claim: Fore-aft spring constant regressions use construction-specific load and pressure coefficients.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
potentialUse: Construction-specific stiffness response and regression tests; coefficients are aircraft-tire-specific and not transferable to racing.

claim: A membrane approximation relates supported vertical load to inflation pressure, deflection and tire geometry.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
potentialUse: Pressure/load/deflection architecture and dimensional checks; not a setup-pressure solver by itself.

claim: Footprint length normalized by diameter is a nonlinear function of normalized vertical deflection.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.

claim: Hysteresis loss ratio is loop energy divided by total loading energy.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
potentialUse: Separate flex/cyclic heat input from slip/friction heat.

claim: Tread-wear driving power is obtained from footprint pressure and local slip-velocity distributions.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
relationshipOriginal: power_intensity(x,y) = contact_pressure(x,y) * local_slip_velocity(x,y); total_power = integral_over_footprint(power_intensity dA)
potentialUse: Evidence-supported wear-energy architecture; requires calibration before AC-vKm mapping.

claim: Mechanical heat input/road resistance obeys power equals drag times speed.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
potentialUse: Energy-conservation gate for friction and hysteresis heat paths.

claim: Model-tire hydroplaning spin-down speed varied approximately with water-film thickness to the minus one-sixth power.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
potentialUse: Wet architecture validation, not dry tire calibration.

claim: Contained-air temperature time histories were represented by second-order least-squares fits.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
relationshipOriginal: T_air(t) fitted with a second-order time function
potentialUse: Validate cavity-temperature time constants without equating cavity and tread sensors.

claim: Cornering response is load-sensitive and pressure-sensitive through deflection and footprint geometry.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
relationshipOriginal: cornering_force_coefficient decreases with rated-load fraction; footprint width decreases with pressure
potentialUse: Load-sensitive grip/stiffness architecture, qualitative outside the source tire.

claim: Flex heat rises strongly beyond the tested nominal deflection range, whereas yaw/slip heat is concentrated near the tread surface.
applicability: General tire-mechanics architecture only; not a racing-family coefficient.
limitations: Aircraft/general-technical test context; construction, scale, load and duty cycle control transfer.
relationshipOriginal: Q_flex increases with carcass deflection; Q_slip increases with yaw/slip and is surface-biased
potentialUse: Keep CARCASS_ROLLING_K and friction/slip heat as separate paths.
